Overview

Kampala as a Business Centre

Kampala is the capital of Uganda and the seat of its government, central bank and main commercial institutions. The Uganda Bureau of Statistics recorded 1,797,722 residents in Kampala Capital City in the 2024 census, across the five divisions of Makindye, Nakawa, Rubaga, Kawempe and Kampala Central, with the wider metropolitan area extending into Wakiso and Mukono. Services account for the largest share of Ugandan output, and Kampala concentrates banking, insurance, telecommunications, trade and professional services. Investment linked to the oil and gas sector, the Standard Gauge Railway and industrial parks such as Namanve has driven demand for offices, warehousing and the companies that serve these projects.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Kampala because most of Uganda's commercial decisions, contracts and disputes pass through the city. International companies entering the oil and gas supply chain or infrastructure projects need to know who owns local partners and whether politically exposed persons sit behind them. Lenders and investors face land risk, where overlapping tenure systems and forged titles can undermine security. Backlogs in the courts mean disputes can run for years, so creditors and litigants need well documented histories of counterparties and their assets. Public procurement through central and city government is a further recurring source of integrity concerns.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Kampala

01

Oil, gas and infrastructure supplier checks

International operators and contractors working on Uganda's oil, gas and railway projects rely on Kampala-registered suppliers and joint venture partners. We trace ownership through URSB records, identify politically exposed persons and related parties, and review litigation and media to support local content and anti-corruption compliance.

02

Land title and mortgage security

Kampala land can be held under mailo, freehold, leasehold or customary tenure, and forged or duplicate titles are a known risk. With local professionals, we help lenders and investors check registered ownership, encumbrances and Land Division litigation before a purchase or loan is secured on Kampala property.

03

Commercial Division litigation support

Banking, insurance, company and insolvency disputes are heard by the Commercial Division of the High Court in Nakasero, which has long carried a significant backlog. We support counsel with counterparty backgrounds, corporate histories and asset research, helping them plan claims, settlements and enforcement over long timelines.

04

Public procurement and integrity reviews

Contracts awarded by ministries, agencies and Kampala Capital City Authority attract scrutiny over conflicts of interest and connected bidders. We examine bidders' ownership, directors and links to officials, and review Anti-Corruption Division judgments and media, to help clients, donors and lenders assess integrity risk.

05

Bank and fintech partner diligence

Kampala is the centre of Uganda's banking, insurance and mobile money sectors. Investors and payment partners entering this market need to understand who controls licensed institutions, agents and fintech firms. We review corporate records, regulatory actions, litigation and adverse media to identify control, conflicts and reputational issues.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Kampala

High Court divisions in Kampala

The High Court of Uganda operates specialised divisions in Kampala. The Commercial Division, established in 1996 and located on Lumumba Avenue in Nakasero, hears company, bankruptcy, intellectual property and other commercial disputes. The Land Division handles land disputes and supervises land tribunals. The Anti-Corruption Division and International Crimes Division, both created in July 2008, sit in Kololo. Reported Commercial Division backlogs, of more than 4,000 cases in a 2020 account, mean disputes can last many years.

Arbitration in Kampala

Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, Cap 5, two institutions act as appointing authorities: the Center for Arbitration and Dispute Resolution (CADER) and the International Centre for Arbitration and Mediation in Kampala (ICAMEK). The Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act 2024 made CADER a department of the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs. A 2025 High Court decision, reported as noting CADER was not yet fully constituted, confirmed that parties may begin arbitration at ICAMEK.

Company and land registries

Companies are registered with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau, headquartered in Kampala, whose searches show directors, shareholders and filed documents; the beneficial ownership register is available to oversight bodies but not to the public. Land records are held by the Ministry of Lands, with Kampala's mix of mailo, freehold, leasehold and customary tenure making searches complex. Local professionals are usually needed to obtain certified search results.

City and national institutions

Kampala Capital City Authority governs the city and runs its own procurement and physical planning functions. The Bank of Uganda, the Inspectorate of Government, the Financial Intelligence Authority and most national regulators are based in Kampala, so regulatory decisions, enforcement actions and corruption investigations affecting Ugandan businesses are generally recorded there. Court judgments are published, often with delays, through the Uganda Legal Information Institute.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Kampala

TDSC has no office in Kampala and works on Kampala matters from its Nashville headquarters. We begin with the client's decision, such as appointing an oil and gas supplier, lending against Kampala property, pursuing a debtor or evaluating a procurement award, and confirm with Ugandan counsel how the Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019 applies to the personal data involved. Research draws on URSB filings, published judgments of the Commercial, Land and Anti-Corruption Divisions, regulatory notices and Ugandan and regional media. Title searches, document retrieval and discreet enquiries are handled by qualified local professionals we coordinate. Reports identify which findings rest on certified records and which on reputational sources.

TDSC has no office in Kampala. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Kampala: Frequently Asked Questions

How do you check land before lending or investing in Kampala?

We coordinate qualified local professionals to obtain search results from the Ministry of Lands registry, check for caveats, mortgages and competing claims, and review Land Division litigation. We also research the seller or borrower and connected companies. Because tenure in Kampala includes mailo, freehold, leasehold and customary land, final title advice should come from Ugandan counsel.

Where are commercial disputes heard in Kampala?

Commercial disputes go to the Commercial Division of the High Court in Nakasero, Kampala, which handles company, insolvency, banking and intellectual property matters. Land disputes go to the Land Division and corruption cases to the Anti-Corruption Division. Arbitration may be administered by ICAMEK. We support counsel with research tailored to the forum.

Can you identify beneficial owners of a Kampala company?

URSB records show directors and registered shareholders, and these are our starting point. The beneficial ownership register filed with URSB is not publicly available, so we look for ownership and control through shareholder chains, related companies, litigation, procurement records and media. We report confidence levels rather than presenting inferred ownership as fact.

Do you support oil and gas local content diligence?

Yes. Operators and contractors often need to vet Kampala-registered suppliers under local content and anti-corruption policies. We research ownership, links to public officials, past contract performance disputes and adverse media, and flag where ownership appears designed to meet local content rules while control lies elsewhere.

Does TDSC have staff in Uganda?

No. TDSC is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Uganda. When work must be done in Kampala, such as registry searches, court file reviews or site visits, we coordinate qualified local professionals and work with Ugandan counsel on what may lawfully be done.
